# notes: Impedance measured in free air (chart title "Free Air Impedance"). 1/12-octave sampling means the resonance peak may fall between points: the sampled maximum can under-read the true peak height and be up to 1/24 octave (2.9%) off in frequency. Chart title verbatim: "Frequency Response on IEC Baffle (DIN45575) @ 1W, 1 m - Free Air Impedance". Sheet sensitivity row verbatim: "Sensitivity@1W,1m" 4 ohm 99.4 dB, 8 ohm 99 dB, 16 ohm 99 dB. The sheet does not state the T/S measurement method, drive level or ambient conditions, nor the voltage behind "1W" (conventionally 2.83 V for 8 ohm, 2.0 V for 4 ohm, 4.0 V for 16 ohm). Uncertainty fields describe transcription only (values are the manufacturer's own numbers, given to 8+ significant figures); the measurement's own uncertainty is unstated. Curve key nominal= is the nominal impedance in ohm of the version measured. Sheet/curve inconsistency: high-Qms driver (Qms 16-20), the sampled curve peak is far below Re+Res (4 ohm: 98 vs 123 ohm; 8 ohm: 118 vs 217; 16 ohm: 199 vs 372 ohm) -- the 1/12-octave sampling (and probable smoothing) cannot resolve a peak whose half-power bandwidth is only Fs/Qms ~ 6-7 Hz; also in the 8 and 16 ohm columns the printed Res (210, 360) is inconsistent with Re*Qms/Qes (129, 232 ohm). Do not fit Qms from this curve's peak height.
